story: In ancient times, seven demigod sages, part man and part fish or bird, were sent to bring wisdom to humanity. Each was paired with a primeval king who ruled before a great flood. The first of these sages, emerging from the sea, taught humans the arts of civilization, including the story of how the world was created. After the flood, further sages and kings were named, though these later sages were considered human and were called by a different title than the seven demigods. The seven sages were entrusted with tablets recording destinies. One of them was said to have made a set of ritual remedies, which another sage carried up to the world above to gain favor. The sages were also credited with founding seven great cities, and with laying the foundations of a renowned city. In one tale, after the flood, the chief god banished the seven sages to the deep waters, declaring that they would not return. Later, a warrior god persuaded the chief god to leave his temple and fetch the sages back himself, promising to keep order in his absence. But while the chief god was away, chaos broke out, and instead of the sages, human experts were given the task of cleansing the god's shrine. One sage was recorded as the author of a myth about a legendary king. The last of the seven was said to have ascended into heaven. Another version of these stories, written later in Greek by a priest, described the first sage rising from the sea to give kings and humans knowledge, including the tale of the world's creation, before further kings ruled until the great flood came.
